title: The Future of Precision Manufacturing Starts with People
summary: Across many of the industries we serve, the rules are changing.The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is driving demand for increasingly sophisticated, printed circuit boards, where laser-drilled hole counts can now reach hundreds of thousands, and in some cases approach a million per board.
body_text: When people think about innovation, they often picture breakthrough technologies or next-generation products. What they do not always see is the combination of customer insight, engineering expertise, manufacturing excellence, and collaboration that makes those breakthroughs possible. Across the industries we serve, requirements are evolving rapidly. The growth of AI infrastructure, advanced electronics, and additive manufacturing is increasing demand for systems that deliver exceptional speed, precision, stability, and reliability. Customers are no longer willing to compromise between performance and accuracy. They expect both. Recognizing this shift, our teams saw an opportunity to rethink what was possible. Rather than pursuing incremental improvements, they undertook a comprehensive redesign of our flagship Lightning™ beam steering platform . Engineers reimagined key elements of the system across mechanics, optics, electronics, and firmware to create a platform designed for the next generation of customer applications. A key contributor to this effort has been Brendan Boyd, Beam Steering R&D Manager, and his team, whose work continues to advance beam steering technologies while helping customers meet increasingly demanding performance requirements. Guided by close collaboration with OEMs and end users, the team evaluates emerging technologies and gathers real-world feedback while refining solutions that create meaningful value for customers . Innovation also extends far beyond product design. Delivering breakthrough performance consistently requires advanced manufacturing processes, sophisticated testing capabilities, automation, and a relentless focus on quality. Through ongoing investments in these areas, we have built manufacturing capabilities that enable precision and scale. Andy Eccles, Manufacturing Engineering Manager, and his team play a critical role in turning innovative designs into products that can be built efficiently and consistently. Advanced fixtures, automated assembly systems, enhanced test equipment, and continuously improving processes help ensure every product performs to the highest standards. Equally important, engineers and operators work closely together to transform practical experience into improvements in efficiency and performance. This commitment to manufacturing excellence has become a meaningful competitive advantage. At the same time, we are building the foundation for future growth across our global manufacturing network. Through modular automation platforms, standardized test systems, and the continued expansion of Fusion, our proprietary manufacturing platform, we are creating a global factory approach that supports traceability and operational excellence across regions. David Keng, Senior Manager, Sustaining & Advanced Engineering, and his automation and test engineering team are helping drive this work by developing scalable automation and digital infrastructure that can be deployed across our manufacturing network. Fusion provides a common digital framework that connects production and test data, improves visibility, accelerates problem-solving, and enables innovations developed in one location to be adopted more quickly across the organization. What makes all of this possible is our people. Engineers, manufacturing specialists, automation experts, operators, quality professionals, and operations teams work together to solve complex challenges and support one another beyond traditional organizational boundaries. The result is more than a new platform or manufacturing capability. It is a stronger foundation for long-term innovation. As we continue strengthening capabilities, we remain focused on investing in what matters most: technical expertise, customer partnership, manufacturing excellence, digital innovation, and a culture of collaboration. Technology may be the outcome, but people make innovation possible. Together, they are helping shape the future of precision manufacturing and building the foundation for our next chapter of growth. By Jens Hupkau, VP of Engineering

title: Robinson Helicopter Company to deliver 5,000th R44 Raven II
summary: The company sold its milestone aircraft to the dealership ARICA in Ecuador.
body_text: Robinson Helicopter Company (RHC) has reached a new milestone, selling its 5,000th R44 Raven II helicopter to its dealership ARICA in Ecuador. This achievement marks a defining moment in the company’s history and reflects steady, global demand for the R44 globally. The R44 is known for its simple design, low operating cost and reliable performance. Pilots and small businesses fly it for training, tours, farm work, news coverage and personal travel. It has become one of the most common helicopters in the sky today. “Delivering the 5,000th r44 +raven+ii" target="_blank"> R44 Raven II reflects the enduring trust operators around the world place in Robinson,” said David Smith, president and CEO of Robinson Helicopter Company. “The R44 remains the most widely sold and flown light civil helicopter on the planet because it delivers unmatched reliability, low direct operating costs, and multi-mission versatility. Whether it is powering flight schools, supporting agricultural operations, or serving private and utility operators, the Raven II is the benchmark for modern light rotorcraft.” Robinson certified the R44 in 1990 and delivered the first R44 in 1993. Since then, the model has grown into one of the best-selling helicopters ever made with owners and operators in more than 100 countries flying it today. The R44 comes in multiple variants, including the Raven I, Clipper I, the Cadet for training and the Raven II and its counterpart the Clipper II. Robinson recently unveiled a new Utility Interior available on all R44s, with easy to clean seat fabrics and replacing the carpet and headliner with a more ruggedized materials for tough missions. This press release was prepared and distributed by Robinson Helicopter Company.

summary: First‑of‑its‑kind demo advances autonomous undersea operationsPORTSMOUTH, R.I., Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, and Composite Energy Technologies (CET) have successfully demonstrated the undersea launch capabilities of HADALUS, a new, low-cost, long-endurance unmanned undersea vehicle (UUV).During a recent U.S. Navy exercise, the UUV completed a series of at-sea missions on a Navy undersea test range, successfully demonstrating its undersea launch capabilities while submerged. body_text: RTX's Raytheon and Composite Energy Technology successfully demonstrate new unmanned undersea vehicle August 10, 2026 Share this article on Facebook Share this article on Twitter Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article via email First ‑ of ‑ its ‑ kind demo advances autonomous undersea operations PORTSMOUTH, R.I. , Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, and Composite Energy Technologies (CET) have successfully demonstrated the undersea launch capabilities of HADALUS, a new, low-cost, long-endurance unmanned undersea vehicle (UUV). During a recent U.S. Navy exercise, the UUV completed a series of at-sea missions on a Navy undersea test range, successfully demonstrating its undersea launch capabilities while submerged. This marks the first time the U.S. Navy has seen this integrated capability in the water and points toward a future where a single unmanned undersea platform can perform detect, reacquire and engage functions within one mission. "This demonstration is an important step in a broader roadmap to deliver autonomous, end‑to‑end undersea capabilities that are far less detectable than surface platforms," said Jen Gauthier, vice president of Naval Systems & Sustainment at Raytheon. "By tightly coupling design, integration and at‑sea experimentation, we've proven we can bring new autonomous solutions to the fleet quickly and cost‑effectively." HADALUS is a 34‑foot UUV with a six‑foot cross section and more than 2,000 nautical miles of endurance. Its free‑flooded, all‑carbon‑fiber exoskeleton delivers exceptional strength and payload capacity while enabling a significantly lower‑cost architecture. Designed to cost roughly one‑third to one‑fifth of comparable long‑endurance vehicles, HADALUS offers a scalable path to fielding affordable undersea capabilities. In less than 18 months, Raytheon and CET progressed from a conceptual sketch to a complete prototype successfully demonstrated in water. This was driven by investment from both companies in the design and build of the vehicle, integration of the launcher, sonar and electronics and full system testing leading up to the exercise. "HADALUS demonstrates that the undersea industrial base can move with greater speed and dynamism than traditional development cycles allow," said Chase Hogoboom, CEO and president of CET. "By combining CET's advanced composite vehicle architecture with Raytheon's mission systems, sensors and integration expertise, we have created a highly capable platform that can be produced at a fraction of the cost of conventional alternatives." Raytheon is significantly expanding its workforce to support critical military programs. Opportunities are available for emerging talent, experienced professionals, and veterans. Discover open roles on our website and apply today. About Raytheon Raytheon, an RTX business, is a leading provider of defense solutions to help the U.S. government, our allies and partners defend their national sovereignty and ensure their security. For more than 100 years, Raytheon has developed new technologies and enhanced existing capabilities in integrated air and missile defense, smart weapons, missiles, advanced sensors and radars, interceptors, space-based systems, hypersonics and missile defense across land, air, sea and space. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact [email protected] .
